text: A well-designed REST API is easy to use and understand. Start by creating clear, meaningful endpoints that represent your resources, such as /users or /orders. Always use the correct HTTP status codes so clients know what happened: 200 for success, 404 when something is not found, and 500 for server errors. Good documentation is essential because it helps developers learn how to use your API quickly. Finally, use versioning, like /v1/users, so you can improve your API without breaking existing applications. Following these simple practices makes your API reliable and pleasant to work with.
